_note: Weirdest Words in Made-Up Languages be like. Same pipeline as untrans (python3 fetch_untrans.py conwords; node untrans.mjs --set conwords). Each word is a real Lingua Libre recording on Commons; the English translation is read by a Piper AI voice, labelled on screen. Ranked 10 -> 1 by the number of English words in the shortest honest translation.
title: Weirdest Words in Made-Up Languages be like
subtitle: RANKED BY HOW MANY ENGLISH WORDS IT TAKES
outro: Which made-up word did we miss?

items.name: Esperanto
items.translation: To speak your own language with Esperanto speakers.
items.fact: It literally means 'to crocodile'. At Esperanto meetings you are meant to speak only Esperanto, and anyone who slips back into their own language gets called a crocodile.

items.name: Toki Pona
items.translation: To interact with the official Toki Pona book.
items.fact: Toki Pona gets by with about 120 words, and it still spends one of them on its own textbook, written by its creator Sonja Lang in 2014.

items.name: Lojban
items.fact: Lojban is built on logic, so feelings get their own tiny sounds that you drop into a sentence. .ua is the exact moment something clicks.

items.name: Láadan
items.fact: Linguist Suzette Haden Elgin invented Láadan in 1982 to give women words other languages lack. It has separate verbs for menstruating in pain, with joy, and for the first time.

items.name: Esperanto
items.fact: Esperanto snaps words together like Lego: sam (same) + ide (idea) + an (member) + o (a noun). A 'same-idea-person' is what Esperanto speakers call each other.

items.name: Lojban
items.fact: Add 'nai' and any feeling flips: .uinai means 'I'm unhappy'. Lojban has dozens of these, like .u'u for 'sorry' and .oi for 'ouch'.

items.name: Toki Pona
items.fact: Almost every Toki Pona word is one or two syllables, like pona (good) and jan (person). Then there is this 15-letter joke word for a raccoon, and fans love it.
